## *HEALTHSYNC: A CONVOLUTIONAL NEURAL NETWORK SYSTEM FOR KELLGREN-LAWRENCE GRADING OF KNEE OSTEOARTHRITIS*

# **CHAPTER 1: INTRODUCTION**

## **1.1. Statement of the Problem**

![][image1]  
**Knee Osteoarthritis (KOA)** is a prevalent chronic musculoskeletal disorder and a leading cause of physical disability. In clinical routines, Bilateral Posterior-Anterior (PA) digital radiography is the standard, cost-effective imaging modality used to evaluate joint structural damage. The severity of KOA is universally quantified using the Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) grading system, an ordinal scale ranging from **Grade 0 (normal) to Grade 4 (severe).**  
Despite its widespread use, manual KL grading by radiologists is highly subjective, leading to significant inter-observer variability. This is particularly problematic in early stages (Grade 0 and 1\) where radiographic features overlap. Therefore, developing a robust, automated Computer-Aided Diagnosis (CAD) system using deep learning to accurately classify KL grades from X-rays is highly necessary. Such a system ensures diagnostic consistency and reduces the workload for medical practitioners.

## **1.2. Research and Application Objectives**

This software engineering thesis focuses on building a complete, end-to-end classification system with the following objectives:

> * Develop an automated image preprocessing pipeline to isolate and extract independent knee joint regions of interest (ROIs) from raw bilateral X-ray images.  
> * Implement and fine-tune two state-of-the-art Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architectures—**DenseNet-121** and **ResNeXt-50**—optimized exclusively for the 5-class KL grading task.  
> * Evaluate and benchmark the models based on classification accuracy and computational efficiency.  
> * Deploy the optimal CNN model into HealthSync, a containerized web-based software application featuring Grad-CAM explainability to support clinical transparency.

## **1.3. Scope and Subject of Study**

**Subject of Study:** Plain bilateral digital grayscale knee radiographs exclusively. No secondary clinical metadata (such as Age, BMI, or WOMAC scores) are utilized in this system.  
**Scope of Application:** The system is strictly engineered as an *Auxiliary Cross-Sectional CAD System*. It is designed to evaluate the static, current state of the knee joint (KL 0-4) at the time of the X-ray capture. It does not perform longitudinal prognosis or predict future disease progression.

# **CHAPTER 2: LITERATURE REVIEW**

## **2.1. Clinical Criteria for Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) Grading**

![][image2]  
The system is designed to recognize the following structural biomarkers defined by the KL scale:

* 

| KL Grade | Clinical Criteria |
| :---: | ----- |
| Grade 0 | Normal joint space width; no osteophytes. |
| Grade 1 | Doubtful narrowing of the joint space; possible marginal osteophytes. |
| Grade 2 | Definite osteophytes present; possible but not definite joint space narrowing. |
| Grade 3 | Moderate, definite joint space narrowing; multiple osteophytes; subchondral sclerosis. |
| Grade 4 | Severe joint space narrowing (bone-on-bone); large osteophytes; marked sclerosis and bone deformation. |

## **2.2. Review of Applied CNN Architectures in KOA Diagnosis**

To establish a comparative baseline, this thesis references the convolutional feature extraction strategies from two prominent studies:

> * **DenseNet-121 Benchmark (Shahid et al., 2025):** This study successfully applied DenseNet-121 for 5-class KL grading. The architecture's dense connectivity allows for continuous feature reuse, which is highly effective in preserving high-frequency details like microscopic osteophytes across deep layers.  
> * **ResNeXt-50 Convolutional Backbone (derived from Tiulpin et al., 2019):** While the original study utilized a complex multi-task approach with clinical data, this thesis explicitly extracts and evaluates only their base CNN backbone concept. By utilizing ResNeXt-50 with attention mechanisms, the model efficiently filters out soft-tissue noise and focuses on bone margins, making it a strong candidate for pure image-based classification.

# **CHAPTER 3: METHODOLOGY AND SYSTEM DESIGN**

## **3.1. Automated Image Preprocessing Pipeline**

### **3.1.1. Knee Detection and ROI Construction**

![][image3]  
To isolate individual knee joints from full-size radiographs, a decoupled spatial localization pipeline utilizing a **YOLOv8** object detector is implemented

To ensure peripheral marginal osteophytes are not truncated during extraction, each raw bounding box ([![][image4]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=w_%7B%5Ctext%7Bbox%7D%7D%2C%20h_%7B%5Ctext%7Bbox%7D%7D#0)) is dynamically expanded into a standardized square **Region of Interest (ROI)** using a scale factor of [![][image5]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Calpha%20%3D%201.15#0):

[![][image6]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ctext%7Bcrop%5C_side%7D%20%3D%201.15%20%5Ctimes%20%5Cmax\(w_%7B%5Ctext%7Bbox%7D%7D%2C%20h_%7B%5Ctext%7Bbox%7D%7D\)#0)

### **3.1.2. Deterministic Classifier Preprocessing**

* **RGB Conversion:** Converts the cropped ROI into the 3-channel RGB color space.  
* **CLAHE Contrast Enhancement:** Converts RGB to LAB space and applies CLAHE ([![][image7]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ctext%7BclipLimit%7D%20%3D%201.25#0), [![][image8]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ctext%7BtileGridSize%7D%20%3D%20\(8%2C%208\)#0)) strictly on the Lightness ([![][image9]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=L#0)) channel to enhance sub-clinical bone features.  
* **Square Padding:** Symmetrically pads any non-square ROI with black pixels ([![][image10]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ctext%7Bvalue%7D%20%3D%200#0)) into a perfect square.  
* **Resizing:** Directly resizes the padded ROI to the target classifier resolution of 384 x 384 pixels.  
* **Tensor Normalization:** Converts the array to a floating-point tensor and normalizes it using standard ImageNet parameters ([![][image11]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Cmu%20%3D%20%5B0.485%2C%200.456%2C%200.406%5D#0), [![][image12]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Csigma%20%3D%20%5B0.229%2C%200.224%2C%200.225%5D#0)):

[![][image13]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Cmathbf%7BX%7D_%7B%5Ctext%7Bnorm%7D%7D%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7B%5Cmathbf%7BX%7D%20-%20%5Cmu%7D%7B%5Csigma%7D#0)

> 

## **3.2. CNN Architectures**

> * **Model A (DenseNet-121):** Leverages dense blocks where each layer receives feature maps from all preceding layers. A custom Fully Connected (FC) head (1024 \-\> 256 \-\> 5\) is attached.  
> * **Model B (ResNeXt-50):** Utilizes grouped convolutions to expand the network's cardinality, capturing diverse anatomical representations without drastically increasing parameter count. A similar FC head is appended.

### **3.2.1. DensetNet-121**

![][image14]

#### **3.2.1.1. Initial Feature Extractor**

* **Input:** Preprocessed knee X-ray images resized to **224 x 224 x 3**.  
* **Processing:** The image passes through an initial Convolutional layer (**Conv** 7 x 7, stride 2\) , followed by **Batch Normalization (BN)**, a **ReLU** activation function, and a **Max Pooling** layer (3 x 3, stride 2).  
* **Purpose:** Rapidly reduces the spatial dimensions to **56 x 56** pixels to smooth the feature maps and reduce computational overhead before entering the main blocks.

#### **3.2.1.2. Dense Blocks & Dense Layers**

DenseNet-121 consists of **4 main Dense Blocks** connected sequentially, each containing multiple **Dense Layers** (or *Bottleneck Layers*):

* **Number of Dense Layers per Block:**  
  * **Dense Block 1:** 6 Dense Layers  
  * **Dense Block 2:** 12 Dense Layers  
  * **Dense Block 3:** 24 Dense Layers  
  * **Dense Block 4:** 16 Dense Layers  
* **Internal Structure of a Dense Layer (Bottleneck):**  
  Each Dense Layer executes a composite transformation sequence [![][image15]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=H_l#0):  
  [![][image16]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ctext%7BBN%7D%20%5Crightarrow%20%5Ctext%7BReLU%7D%20%5Crightarrow%20%5Ctext%7BConv%20%7D%20\(1%20%5Ctimes%201\)%20%5Crightarrow%20%5Ctext%7BBN%7D%20%5Crightarrow%20%5Ctext%7BReLU%7D%20%5Crightarrow%20%5Ctext%7BConv%20%7D%20\(3%20%5Ctimes%203\)#0)  
  * The **Conv 1 x 1** layer acts as a bottleneck to reduce the number of feature channels, optimizing computational efficiency.  
  * The **Conv  3 x 3** layer extracts spatial anatomical features (such as marginal osteophytes and joint space boundaries).  
* **Feature Concatenation Mechanism:** The output of the [![][image17]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=l%5E%7B%5Ctext%7Bth%7D%7D#0) Dense Layer is concatenated with its input feature maps:  
   [![][image18]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=x_l%20%3D%20H_l\(%5Bx_0%2C%20x_1%2C%20x_2%2C%20%5Cdots%2C%20x_%7Bl-1%7D%5D\)#0)  
  This mechanism promotes feature reuse , alleviates the vanishing-gradient problem, and preserves subtle micro-anatomical details across deeper layers.

#### **3.2.1.3. Transition Layers**

Located between consecutive Dense Blocks, **Transition Layers** regulate the dimensions of the feature maps:

* **Structure:** Composed of **Conv  1 x 1** layer followed by an **Average Pooling** layer (2 x 2, stride 2).  
* **Purpose:** Reduces the number of feature channels via a compression factor [![][image19]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ctheta%20%5Cle%201#0) and halves the spatial dimensions ([![][image20]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=H%20%5Ctimes%20W#0)) before feeding feature maps into the next Dense Block.

#### **3.2.1.4. Classification Head (Fully Connected Layers)**

After feature extraction through Dense Block 4 , the feature maps are passed to a custom classification head:

* **Global Average Pooling (GAP):** Flattens the feature maps into a 1D vector (dimension 1024).  
* **Fully Connected (FC) Head:** The vector passes through fully connected layers with **ReLU** activations , **Dropout** ([![][image21]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=p%20%3D%200.3#0)) , and **L2 Weight Regularization** ([![][image22]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Clambda%20%3D%201%20%5Ctimes%2010%5E%7B-4%7D#0)) to prevent overfitting.  
* **Output Layer (Softmax):** The final output layer consists of 5 neurons corresponding to the Kellgren-Lawrence severity grades (KL Grade 0–4) , producing probability distributions via the Softmax function.

### **3.2.2. SE-ResNeXt-50 32x4d**

#### **3.2.2.1. ResNeXt Convolutional Branch (Split-Transform-Merge)**![][image23]

The main branch accepts the input feature map [![][image24]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=X%20%5Cin%20%5Cmathbb%7BR%7D%5E%7BH%20%5Ctimes%20W%20%5Ctimes%20C_%7B%5Ctext%7Bin%7D%7D%7D#0) and applies a sequence of three convolutional transformations:

* **First 1 x 1 Conv Layer (Bottleneck Reduction):**  
  * **Function:** Compresses the number of channels from [![][image25]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=C_%7B%5Ctext%7Bin%7D%7D#0) (e.g., 256\) down to an intermediate bottleneck width [![][image26]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=C_%7B%5Ctext%7Bmid%7D%7D%20%3D%20128#0) (corresponding to 32 x 4d}).  
  * **Objective:** Reduces computational complexity for the subsequent spatial convolution layer.  
* **3 x 3  Grouped Conv Layer (Grouped Convolution):**  
  * **Function:** Splits the compressed [![][image27]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=C_%7B%5Ctext%7Bmid%7D%7D#0) channels into **32 independent groups (C \= 32\)**, where each group computes convolutions across **4 channels (d \= 4\)**.  
  * **Objective:** Instead of processing feature maps in a single high-dimensional space, dividing feature extraction across 32 parallel paths allows the model to learn diverse geometric representations of bone margins, osteophytes, and joint spaces from multiple viewpoints without increasing overall parameter size.  
* **Second 1 x1  Conv Layer (Bottleneck Expansion):**  
  * **Function:** Expands the channel capacity from [![][image28]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=C_%7B%5Ctext%7Bmid%7D%7D#0) (128) back to the target output dimension [![][image29]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=C_%7B%5Ctext%7Bout%7D%7D#0) (256).  
  * **Objective:** Ensures the channel dimension matches the identity shortcut (X) for subsequent element-wise addition.

#### **3.2.2.2. Channel Attention Module (Squeeze-and-Excitation \- SE Module)**

![][image30]

1. **Squeeze Operation:**  
   Applies **Global Average Pooling** to condense spatial dimensions (H x W) into a 1 x 1 x C channel descriptor vector z:  
     
   [![][image31]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=z_c%20%3D%20F_%7B%5Ctext%7Bsq%7D%7D\(u_c\)%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7BH%20%5Ctimes%20W%7D%20%5Csum_%7Bi%3D1%7D%5E%7BH%7D%20%5Csum_%7Bj%3D1%7D%5E%7BW%7D%20u_c\(i%2C%20j\)#0)  
     
   *Significance:* Captures the global contextual information across each feature channel c.  
     
2. **Excitation Operation:**  
   Feeds the vector z through two Fully Connected (FC) layers with a reduction ratio r (typically r \= 16), utilizing a **ReLU** activation in between and a **Sigmoid** activation at the output:  
     
   *Significance:* Learns non-linear interactions between channels to generate channel-wise weight scales [![][image32]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=s%20%5Cin%20%5B0%2C%201%5D%5EC#0).  
     
3. **Scale Operation:**  
   Multiplies the learned activation weights [![][image33]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=s_c#0) element-wise back onto the original feature map [![][image34]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=u_c#0):  
     
   [![][image35]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ctilde%7Bx%7D_c%20%3D%20F_%7B%5Ctext%7Bscale%7D%7D\(u_c%2C%20s_c\)%20%3D%20s_c%20%5Ccdot%20u_c#0)  
     
   *Significance:* Channels containing critical medical diagnostic features (e.g., joint space narrowing) are adaptively amplified, while irrelevant or noisy background channels are suppressed.  
   

#### **3.2.2.3. Identity Skip Connection & Residual Fusion**

* **Identity Skip Connection:** Passes the original input X directly around the convolutional transformations, preventing gradient degradation (*vanishing gradient*) in deep network layers.  
* **Residual Fusion ([![][image36]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Coplus#0)):** The recalibrated output tensor [![][image37]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ctilde%7BX%7D#0) from the SE Module is added directly (*element-wise addition*) to the original input tensor [![][image38]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=X#0):  
  [![][image39]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ctext%7BOutput%7D%20%3D%20%5Ctext%7BReLU%7D\(%5Ctilde%7BX%7D%20%2B%20X\)#0)  
* **Final Activation:** Passes through a final **ReLU** activation function before being transmitted to the subsequent block in the network.

## **3.3. Loss Function and Optimization**

### **Cross-Entropy (CE) Loss**

The standard **Categorical Cross-Entropy (CE)** loss treats all KL grades as completely independent categorical classes. It penalizes the difference between the true one-hot encoded label distribution [![][image40]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=y#0) and the predicted probability distribution [![][image41]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Chat%7By%7D#0) produced by the Softmax function:

[![][image42]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Cmathcal%7BL%7D_%7B%5Ctext%7BCE%7D%7D%20%3D%20-%5Csum_%7Bc%3D0%7D%5E%7BK-1%7D%20y_c%20%5Clog\(%5Chat%7By%7D_c\)#0)

* **Where:**   
  * [![][image43]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=K%20%3D%205#0) is the total number of KL grades (0 to 4).  
  * [![][image44]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=y_c%20%5Cin%20%5C%7B0%2C%201%5C%7D#0) is a binary indicator of whether class label [![][image45]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=c#0) is the correct classification for the observation.  
  * [![][image46]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Chat%7By%7D_c#0) is the predicted probability for class [![][image47]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=c#0).

## **3.4. Dataset preparation**

### **3.4.1. Knee Joint ROI Detection Dataset**

![][image3]  
To train the **YOLOv8** object detection model to automatically detect and extract bounding boxes for both knee joints from bilateral radiographs, a specialized, manually annotated dataset was constructed:

* **Data Source:** A total of 1,500 raw bilateral posterior-anterior (PA) X-ray images were retrieved from the public [Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI)](https://nda.nih.gov/oai) database.  
* **Annotation & Management (Roboflow):** The raw radiographs were ingested into the **Roboflow** platform for manual bounding-box annotation. Each image was annotated with precise bounding boxes delineating the left and right knee joint Regions of Interest (ROIs).  
* **Data Partitioning:** The annotated dataset of 1,500 images was partitioned using a standard **80 : 10 : 10** split ratio:  
  * **Train Set:** 1,200 images (used for YOLOv8 weight optimization).  
  * **Validation Set:** 150 images (used for hyperparameter tuning and model selection).  
  * **Test Set:** 150 images   
* **Objective:** Ensures the YOLOv8 detector achieves high spatial accuracy and robustness against varying image contrasts and minor patient alignment deviations.

### **3.4.2. Knee Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) Grading Dataset**

![][image48]  
Following automated ROI isolation and cropping, the multi-class classification backbones (DenseNet-121 and SE-ResNeXt-50) were trained on a public benchmark dataset from Kaggle: [Knee Osteoarthritis Dataset with Severity](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/shashwatwork/knee-osteoarthritis-dataset-with-severity).

* **Data Source:** The dataset consists of pre-cropped knee joint radiographs derived from the OAI cohort, pre-labeled into 5 distinct Kellgren-Lawrence severity grades (0 \-\> 4).  
* **Class Distribution:**  
  The dataset comprises a total of **9,750 cropped knee joint images**, distributed across the five KL grades as follows:  
  * **KL Grade 0 (Normal):** 3,857 images  
  * **KL Grade 1 (Doubtful / Minimal):** 1,762 images  
  * **KL Grade 2 (Mild):** 2,578 images  
  * **KL Grade 3 (Moderate):** 1,286 images  
  * **KL Grade 4 (Severe):** 267 images  
* **Data Partitioning:** The images are organized into fixed **Training**, **Validation**, and **Test** directories to maintain experimental reproducibility across model architectures.

### **3.4.3. Pair view Yolo dataset**

For each **full radiograph**, YOLOv8 detects one or more knee joints. Each detection is converted into a classifier image using this deterministic procedure:

1. Read the detector box in source-image pixel coordinates.  
2. Set the square side to **1.15 \* max(box width, box height)**.  
   Keep the square centered on the detected box so both joint margins and marginal osteophytes remain visible.

## **3.5. Training Methodology**

### **3.5.1. Class Balancing**

The training loader uses a full inverse-frequency WeightedRandomSampler:

* sampler power: 1.0  
* replacement: enabled  
* sampled epoch length: equal to the training-set length  
* minority-only augmentation: **disabled**

### **3.5.2. Data Augmentation**

| Operation | Setting |
| :---- | :---- |
| Horizontal flip | probability 0.50 |
| Rotation | \+/-5 degrees |
| Brightness jitter | 0.08 |
| Contrast jitter | 0.08 |
| Random erasing | probability 0.10 |
| Erasing scale | 0.02-0.05 |
| Erasing ratio | 0.5-2.0 |

### **3.5.3. Optimization and Regularization**

* **Optimizer Selection:** Evaluated **AdamW**. AdamW is utilized in early stages for rapid convergence  
* **Learning Rate Scheduling:** Applies **Cosine Annealing**, smoothly decaying the learning rate from [![][image49]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ceta_%7B%5Ctext%7Bmax%7D%7D#0) to [![][image50]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ceta_%7B%5Ctext%7Bmin%7D%7D#0) following a cosine curve:  
  ![][image51]  
  [![][image52]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ceta_t%20%3D%20%5Ceta_%7B%5Ctext%7Bmin%7D%7D%20%2B%20%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B2%7D\(%5Ceta_%7B%5Ctext%7Bmax%7D%7D%20-%20%5Ceta_%7B%5Ctext%7Bmin%7D%7D\)%5Cleft\(1%20%2B%20%5Ccos%5Cleft\(%5Cfrac%7Bt%7D%7BT_%7B%5Ctext%7Bmax%7D%7D%7D%5Cpi%5Cright\)%5Cright\)#0)

### **3.5.4.  Base Three-Stage Training**

| Stage | Epochs | Trainable parameters | Learning rate | Weight decay | Scheduler |
| :---- | ----: | :---- | :---- | ----: | :---- |
| Head warm-up | 5 | linear classifier | head 3e-4 | 1e-4 | none |
| Coarse fine-tuning | 15 | dense blocks 3-4, norm5, classifier | backbone 3e-5; head 3e-4 | 1e-4 | cosine to 1e-7 |
| Full fine-tuning | 10 | complete network, restarted from best coarse weights | 1e-5 | 1e-3 | cosine to 1e-7 |

Checkpoints are selected using validation only:

**selection \= 0.55 \* QWK \+ 0.30 \* macro\_F1 \+ 0.15 \* macro\_AP**

### **3.5.5. Paired-View Production Adaptation**

| Parameter | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| Loss | CE |
| Epochs | 5 |
| Batch size | 48 |
| Optimizer | AdamW |
| Learning rate | 1e-5 |
| Weight decay | 1e-3 |
| Scheduler | cosine annealing to 1e-7 |
| Gradient clipping | 1.0 |
| ROI expansion | 1.15 |
| Selected epoch | 4  |

Validation evaluates published crops and fixed production YOLO ROIs separately. The robust selection score is the mean of both domains' **0.55 QWK \+ 0.30 macro F1 \+ 0.15 macro AP** scores.

## **3.6. Headmap Methodology**

![][image53]

**Grad-CAM** generalizes CAM to arbitrary CNN architectures by utilizing feature gradients instead of requiring a strict GAP-based classifier.

![][image54]

1. **Forward Pass:** The input image passes through the CNN to yield **Activation Maps ([![][image55]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=A%5Ek#0))** from the final convolutional layer and the target score [![][image56]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=y%5Ec#0) (prior to Softmax).  
2. **Gradient Computation:** Calculates the gradients [![][image57]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Cfrac%7B%5Cpartial%20y%5Ec%7D%7B%5Cpartial%20A%5Ek%7D#0) of the score [![][image58]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=y%5Ec#0) with respect to feature maps [![][image59]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=A%5Ek#0) to produce **Gradient Maps**.  
3. **Global Average Pooling:** Condenses the gradient maps to compute channel importance weights [![][image60]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Calpha_k%5Ec#0):  
   [![][image61]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Calpha_k%5Ec%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7BZ%7D%20%5Csum_%7Bi%7D%20%5Csum_%7Bj%7D%20%5Cfrac%7B%5Cpartial%20y%5Ec%7D%7B%5Cpartial%20A_%7Bi%2Cj%7D%5Ek%7D#0)  
4. **Weighted Combination & ReLU:** Multiplies activation maps [![][image62]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=A%5Ek#0) by weights [![][image63]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Calpha_k%5Ec#0), sums them, and passes the output through a **ReLU** function to generate the final **Grad-CAM Heatmap**:  
   [![][image64]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ctext%7BHeatmap%7D%20%3D%20%5Ctext%7BReLU%7D%5Cleft\(%20%5Csum_%7Bk%7D%20%5Calpha_k%5Ec%20A%5Ek%20%5Cright\)#0)

## **3.7. Evaluation Metrics and Assessment Criteria** 

#### **3.7.1. Primary Clinical Metric: Quadratic Weighted Kappa (QWK)**

**Quadratic Weighted Kappa ([![][image65]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ckappa#0))** is the primary evaluation metric for ordinal classification in medical imaging. It measures inter-rater agreement between the model predictions ([![][image66]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Chat%7By%7D#0)) and ground-truth expert labels ([![][image67]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=y#0)), applying a quadratic penalty based on the distance between predicted and actual grades:

[![][image68]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ckappa%20%3D%201%20-%20%5Cfrac%7B%5Csum_%7Bi%3D0%7D%5E%7BK-1%7D%20%5Csum_%7Bj%3D0%7D%5E%7BK-1%7D%20w_%7Bi%2Cj%7D%20O_%7Bi%2Cj%7D%7D%7B%5Csum_%7Bi%3D0%7D%5E%7BK-1%7D%20%5Csum_%7Bj%3D0%7D%5E%7BK-1%7D%20w_%7Bi%2Cj%7D%20E_%7Bi%2Cj%7D%7D#0)  
Where:

* [![][image69]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=O_%7Bi%2Cj%7D#0) represents the **observed confusion matrix** count for true grade [![][image70]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=i#0) predicted as grade [![][image71]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=j#0).  
* [![][image72]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=E_%7Bi%2Cj%7D#0) represents the expected c**onfusion matrix under statistical independence.**   
  [![][image73]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=E_%7Bi%2Cj%7D%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7BR_i%20%5Ctimes%20C_j%7D%7BN%7D#0)  
    
* [![][image74]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=w_%7Bi%2Cj%7D%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7B\(i%20-%20j\)%5E2%7D%7B\(K%20-%201\)%5E2%7D#0) is the quadratic penalty weight (k \= 5 classes).  
* *Clinical Value:* Heavily penalizes severe diagnostic errors (e.g., mistaking KL Grade 0 for KL Grade 4\) compared to minor adjacent-grade shifts (e.g., KL Grade 1 vs. KL Grade 2).

#### 

#### **3.7.2. Per-Class Precision, Recall (Sensitivity), and Specificity**

To evaluate model reliability across each individual KL grade [![][image75]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=c%20%5Cin%20%5C%7B0%2C%201%2C%202%2C%203%2C%204%5C%7D#0), class-specific binary metrics are computed using True Positives ([![][image76]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ctext%7BTP%7D_c#0)), False Positives ([![][image77]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ctext%7BFP%7D_c#0)), True Negatives ([![][image78]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ctext%7BTN%7D_c#0)), and False Negatives ([![][image79]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ctext%7BFN%7D_c#0)):

1. **Precision (Positive Predictive Value):** Measures the proportion of correctly identified cases among all images predicted as grade [![][image80]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=c#0):  
   [![][image81]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ctext%7BPrecision%7D_c%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7B%5Ctext%7BTP%7D_c%7D%7B%5Ctext%7BTP%7D_c%20%2B%20%5Ctext%7BFP%7D_c%7D#0)  
2. **Recall / Sensitivity (True Positive Rate):** Measures the model's capacity to detect true instances of grade c without missing diagnoses (critical for severe KL 3/4 stages):  
   [![][image82]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ctext%7BRecall%7D_c%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7B%5Ctext%7BTP%7D_c%7D%7B%5Ctext%7BTP%7D_c%20%2B%20%5Ctext%7BFN%7D_c%7D#0)  
3. **Specificity (True Negative Rate):** Quantifies the model's ability to correctly rule out healthy knees or incorrect severity levels:  
   [![][image83]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ctext%7BSpecificity%7D_c%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7B%5Ctext%7BTN%7D_c%7D%7B%5Ctext%7BTN%7D_c%20%2B%20%5Ctext%7BFP%7D_c%7D#0)

#### **3.7.3. Aggregate F1-Scores (Macro and Weighted F1)**

![][image84]

The **F1-Score** is the harmonic mean of Precision and Recall. To handle severe class distribution skewness, two averaging strategies are employed:

* **Macro F1-Score ([![][image85]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=F1_%7B%5Ctext%7Bmacro%7D%7D#0)):** Calculates the unweighted mean of F1-scores across all 5 classes, treating minority classes equally:  
  [![][image86]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=F1_%7B%5Ctext%7Bmacro%7D%7D%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7BK%7D%20%5Csum_%7Bc%3D0%7D%5E%7BK-1%7D%20%5Cfrac%7B2%20%5Ccdot%20%5Ctext%7BPrecision%7D_c%20%5Ccdot%20%5Ctext%7BRecall%7D_c%7D%7B%5Ctext%7BPrecision%7D_c%20%2B%20%5Ctext%7BRecall%7D_c%7D#0)  
* **Weighted F1-Score ([![][image87]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=F1_%7B%5Ctext%7Bweighted%7D%7D#0)):** Weights the F1-score of each class by its support [![][image88]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=N_c#0) (sample count), reflecting total population accuracy:  
  [![][image89]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=F1_%7B%5Ctext%7Bweighted%7D%7D%20%3D%20%5Csum_%7Bc%3D0%7D%5E%7BK-1%7D%20%5Cleft\(%20%5Cfrac%7BN_c%7D%7BN%7D%20%5Ccdot%20F1_c%20%5Cright\)#0)

#### **3.7.4. Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC), Average Precision (AP) and Confusion Matrix** 

For threshold-independent probability evaluation, One-vs-Rest (OvR) curves are plotted for each KL grade:

![][image90]

1. **Area Under Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC-ROC):**  
     
   Evaluates the trade-off between True Positive Rate ([![][image91]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ctext%7BRecall%7D_c#0)) and False Positive Rate ([![][image92]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=1%20-%20%5Ctext%7BSpecificity%7D_c#0)) across all decision thresholds. A high AUC ([![][image93]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=0%20%5Crightarrow%201#0)) reflects superior overall class separability.  
   [![][image94]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ctext%7BAUC%7D%20%3D%20%5Cint_%7B0%7D%5E%7B1%7D%20%5Ctext%7BTPR%7D\(t\)%20%5C%2C%20d\(%5Ctext%7BFPR%7D\(t\)\)#0)  
2. **Average Precision (AP) / Area Under Precision-Recall Curve (PR-AUC):**  
     
   Summarizes the Precision-Recall curve by taking the weighted mean of precisions achieved at each threshold [![][image95]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=n#0):  
     
   [![][image96]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ctext%7BAP%7D_c%20%3D%20%5Csum_%7Bn%7D%20\(%5Ctext%7BRecall%7D_n%20-%20%5Ctext%7BRecall%7D_%7Bn-1%7D\)%20%5Ccdot%20%5Ctext%7BPrecision%7D_n#0)  
   * *Clinical Value:* Provides a much more reliable assessment than AUC-ROC for highly imbalanced classes (specifically KL Grade 4).

	3\. **Confusion Matrix** 

The **Confusion Matrix** is a 5 x 5 square matrix that compares ground-truth expert annotations ([![][image97]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=y#0)) against model predictions ([![][image98]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Chat%7By%7D#0)). For any target grade c, the matrix entries are aggregated into four core diagnostic components:

* **True Positive ([![][image99]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ctext%7BTP%7D_c#0)):** Correctly identified images belonging to grade [![][image100]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=c#0).  
* **False Positive ([![][image101]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ctext%7BFP%7D_c#0)):** Images of other grades incorrectly classified as grade [![][image102]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=c#0) (False Alarms).  
* **True Negative ([![][image103]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ctext%7BTN%7D_c#0)):** Correctly identified images not belonging to grade $c$.  
* **False Negative ([![][image104]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=%5Ctext%7BFN%7D_c#0)):** Images belonging to grade [![][image105]](https://saxarona.github.io/mathjax-viewer/?input=c#0) misclassified as another grade (Missed Diagnoses).

# **CHAPTER 5: SOFTWARE ARCHITECTURE AND DEPLOYMENT**

## **5.1. System Architecture**

As a software engineering project, the finalized CNN model is integrated into **HealthSync**, a distributed web application designed for modern cloud infrastructure:

> * **Backend & AI Inference Service:** Built using Java and Python (FastAPI). The inference service loads the serialized \`.pth\` weights, processes the incoming image through the preprocessing pipeline, and executes a forward pass to return the Softmax probabilities and Grad-CAM array.  
> * **Frontend Web Interface:** A responsive UI allowing medical staff to upload X-rays and view the AI's classification alongside the overlaid heatmap.  
> * **Containerization (DevOps):** The entire application is containerized using Docker, ensuring environmental consistency and enabling seamless CI/CD pipeline integration and deployment onto cloud platforms (AWS / Viettel IDC).

## **5.3. Conclusion**

The HealthSync project successfully delivers a highly accurate, single-task CNN pipeline for evaluating Kellgren-Lawrence grades directly from X-rays. By avoiding overly complex multi-task formulations and focusing purely on robust image feature extraction (DenseNet/ResNeXt) paired with modern software engineering deployment practices (Docker/FastAPI), the system serves as a highly practical, fast, and transparent diagnostic aid for clinical environments.
